artifacts.summary: All 6 phases completed: stale-fixture fix (3 suites), end-of-run failure roster, regression test, known-failures.txt baseline manifest with EXPECTED/NEW classification and --fail-on-new, --skip-slow on all 5 redeploy-checkpoint call sites (measured 13m48s -> 2m4s), and documentation reconciliation.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed the agent-system test harness's three named defects: failing suites are now named in a consolidated, regression-tested end-of-run roster; a committed known-failures.txt baseline classifies each failure as EXPECTED or NEW; and --skip-slow on all five deploy_findings_snapshot call sites removed the dominant wall-clock cost (measured 85% reduction, 13m48s to 2m4s per invocation). Also fixed a shared stale-fixture bug that accounted for 3 of the 8 originally-named failures.

memory_candidates.content: run-all.sh test suites that resolve their subject-under-test via a `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` + deploy-tree-first/source-store-fallback pattern (preferring $REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/... over the source-store sibling) are NOT redundant with a dispatched agent's own pre-deploy phase-gate run: they test the stale deployed copy pre-deploy and only test the fresh copy post-deploy. Roughly 40 of ~73 core test suites use this pattern (grep for 'REPO_ROOT.*\.claude/scripts' in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/). Before removing or deferring a gate-8-style check as 'redundant', confirm whether the suites in question resolve against source or deployed paths — the redundancy argument only holds for the latter's mirror image (source-only suites).

When a checked-in advisory manifest classifies test-harness output (e.g. EXPECTED vs. NEW failures), design the tally/roster extension so the pre-manifest prefix stays byte-identical and the annotation is a pure suffix/append -- this lets an existing regression test's substring/prefix assertions keep working unmodified across the manifest-aware extension, verified in this task by re-running the Phase 3 regression suite unchanged after Phase 4 landed and seeing all cases still pass.

user_decision.question: This task added --skip-slow to all 5 orchestrator redeploy-checkpoint deploy_findings_snapshot call sites, removing the dominant measured wall-clock cost (13m48s -> 2m4s per invocation). During implementation, research turned up that a prior task in this repo (documented in batch-orchestration-guardrails.md's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint section) had already investigated and REJECTED a weaker version of this same idea (sharing one Gate-8 capture between pre/post) because ~40 of ~73 core test suites resolve their subject-under-test from the DEPLOYED tree, not source-store -- meaning this checkpoint's full-depth pair was the only thing verifying those suites pass against a freshly-deployed tree. This task's --skip-slow change is a stricter version: those ~40 suites now get zero coverage from this checkpoint against a fresh deploy. Should this trade-off be accepted as implemented, or should Phase 5 be reverted (restoring the wall-clock cost) pending a narrower follow-up fix?
options: Accept as implemented -- keep --skip-slow on all 5 call sites; the measured wall-clock win (a single dispatch previously consumed ~45 minutes and terminated without writing its handoff) is judged to dominate the residual gap, which is now flagged in code comments, shell-script-testing.md, batch-orchestration-guardrails.md, and this summary's Follow-ups for a scoped future fix

Revert Phase 5 (drop --skip-slow from all 5 call sites, restoring the full-depth pre/post pair and its ~13m48s cost per invocation) until a narrower fix -- running only the ~40 deploy-tree-first suites against gate 8 post-redeploy -- is built as a separate follow-up task
user_decision.recommended: Accept as implemented -- keep --skip-slow on all 5 call sites; the measured wall-clock win (a single dispatch previously consumed ~45 minutes and terminated without writing its handoff) is judged to dominate the residual gap, which is now flagged in code comments, shell-script-testing.md, batch-orchestration-guardrails.md, and this summary's Follow-ups for a scoped future fix
